cases.rationale: Removing the owner guard permits token-a + GET /documents?id=b to return bob-private. Source includes identity mapping, attacker-controlled query and document store; the runtime framework invoking exported handle is assumed. No runtime reproduction claimed.
Adding owner check prevents cross-user document reading on shown handle path. This fixes an earlier defect. Do not report the BASE vulnerability as introduced by this PR.

Object spread order lets token-a request X-Principal:bob override authenticated alice. Listed internal profile service trusts X-Principal and returns bob private email. Identity/caller control are in primary HTTP source. Deployment mapping is static and actual downstream dispatch remains a condition.

Same header-order diff, but downstream derives actor from Authorization token independently and ignores X-Principal. token-a with forged X-Principal:bob still selects alice. No new private-data exposure on this route; upstream header pollution alone is not demonstrated harmful.
Explicit limit20 preserves downstream default20; service enforces integer1..20. Missing caller/runtime is a coverage gap, not evidence of compatibility regression or resource exhaustion.

Unchanged eval(expression) is dangerous and reachable in BASE/HEAD. Changing only a constant log message changes neither evaluation nor input flow. Do not attribute this historical flaw as a new PR finding; separate existing-risk context if desired.
